test.name: Spec 0010 spike: spool with O_RDWR reader and page-size punch

expected: with the reader opened O_RDWR|O_NOFOLLOW and punches aligned to the VM page size, the AC-12 load keeps spool allocation bounded far below the bytes written, SEEK_DATA gives the first unreleased byte, and every line arrives whole and in order (spec 0010 AC-12 feasibility)
actual: Page size (sysconf _SC_PAGESIZE) is 16384. 40-punch experiment: allocation stays at 4096 B and SEEK_DATA equals the released offset after every punch (0 of 40 stale); 64 KiB alignment works too. AC-12 load, fake at 2000 lines/s for 60 s (6016255 and 6016100 B written, 60129 and 60158 log lines, 0 torn or out of order): per stream at most 1052672 B allocated (about 1 MiB beyond the unreleased bytes, flat from t=15 s to t=60 s, not growing), combined at most 2105344 B; SEEK_DATA after the run equals the released offset 6012928 on both streams; resuming as a restarted daemon from SEEK_DATA and dropping to the first newline (17 B) gives a whole line. A rerun with fsync after every punch gave the same 1052672 B per stream. A no-punch control allocated at most 61440 B beyond EOF. Caveat for AC-12's number: per spool file the allocation stays near 1 MiB, but both spools together reached 2105344 B, 8 KiB over 2 MiB (2064384 B in an earlier run), so 'under 2 MiB' holds per spool, not for the two together.

Test root under the darwin user temp folder (confstr _CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR) at stackly-spike0010-<pid>/Test Root Ünï cödé, fake runtime copied to runtime/fake/0.1.0/aarch64-apple-darwin/0f1e2d3c/bin/stackly-fake-server and spawned by its canonical path, data and instance.lock under data/instances/<name>/, spools under run/i/<name>/.
